question: A 38-year-old woman presents with 8 months of symmetrical MCP and PIP joint swelling with 90-minute morning stiffness. Rheumatoid factor (RF) is positive. Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibody testing is ordered. Which statement BEST describes the diagnostic value of anti-CCP in rheumatoid arthritis?

answers.text: Anti-CCP has higher sensitivity than RF and is positive in virtually all RA patients.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Anti-CCP sensitivity (~70%) is similar to or slightly lower than RF (~80%). Its strength lies in its high specificity (~95–98%), not sensitivity.

answers.text: Anti-CCP has high specificity (~95%) for RA and may be positive years before clinical disease onset.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Anti-CCP specificity for RA is approximately 95–98%, making it far more specific than RF (~80%). Critically, anti-CCP antibodies can appear years before clinical synovitis, enabling earlier diagnosis. Their presence also predicts a more erosive disease course.

answers.text: A positive anti-CCP in the absence of RF rules out seronegative RA.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Anti-CCP is independent of RF serology. A patient can be RF-negative but anti-CCP positive; this still represents seropositive RA (anti-CCP positivity is itself a seropositive marker). Seronegative RA means both RF and anti-CCP are negative.

answers.text: Anti-CCP is equally elevated in AS and PsA, limiting its specificity for RA.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Anti-CCP is characteristically negative in AS and PsA (seronegative spondyloarthropathies). A positive anti-CCP strongly favours RA over these conditions, which is precisely its high-specificity value.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the serology of RA: anti-CCP specificity ~95% (higher than RF ~80%), sensitivity ~70%. It is negative in AS and PsA, and can precede clinical symptoms by years.
Excellent. Remember: anti-CCP = high SPECIFICITY (~95%), can precede disease, and predicts erosive course — contrasted with RF which has higher sensitivity but lower specificity.
